memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'But when all goes well with you, remember me and show me kindness; mention me to Pharaoh and get me out of this prison. I was forcibly carried off from the land of the Hebrews, and even here I have done nothing to deserve being put in a dungeon.'" - Gen 40:14-15 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Having given the cupbearer good news, Joseph makes a heartfelt appeal: "When all goes well with you, remember me... mention me to Pharaoh and get me out of this prison." And he explains, honestly, that he had been wronged — kidnapped from his homeland and imprisoned though he had done nothing to deserve it. It is a raw, human cry from a man longing for freedom.

Joseph's request teaches us something healthy. He trusted God completely, yet he also took reasonable steps to seek his release. Faith is not passive fatalism that refuses to lift a finger; it is possible to trust God fully and still ask for help, still use the doors that open before us. Joseph did both — he pointed the cupbearer to God's interpretation, and he asked the man to remember him.

Notice too Joseph's honesty about his suffering. He does not pretend everything is fine or hide his pain. He plainly states that he has been wronged and longs to be free. There is nothing unspiritual about honestly acknowledging our hardships and our desire for relief.

So it is right for us to pray, to trust God, and also to seek help, to knock on doors, to ask people for kindness. Trusting God and taking wise action are not opposites; they belong together. Bring your longings honestly before God, and use the means He provides — while leaving the outcome in His hands.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I balance trusting God with taking reasonable action?
2. Am I honest with God about my hardships and longings?
3. Where might God be providing a "door" I should walk through?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, help me to trust You fully while also taking wise steps and seeking help. I bring my longings honestly before You, and I leave the outcome in Your hands. Amen.
